title: Reconstruct Itinerary
summary: Given a list of airline tickets, reconstruct the departure and arrival airports in order starting from 'JFK'.
statement: Given a list of airline tickets, reconstruct the departure and arrival airports in order starting from 'JFK'. Return the itinerary with the smallest lexical order. Assume all tickets form at least one valid itinerary and use each ticket exactly once.
constraints: 1–300 tickets; each [origin,destination] contains two different three-uppercase-letter airport codes.

Start at JFK and use EVERY ticket occurrence exactly once. Repeated tickets are separate flights. At least one complete itinerary exists; return the lexicographically smallest complete airport sequence.
hints: Tickets are directed edges; the route must traverse every edge once, including duplicate edges.
Use an Euler-trail construction. Explore smallest destinations first, but record an airport only after all outgoing edges are consumed.
Keep a stack starting at JFK. Push the smallest unused outgoing destination; if none remains, pop into a reverse route. Reverse at the end.
Sorting destination lists in reverse order lets pop() take the smallest. Postorder places dead ends at the end instead of prematurely committing them.
editorial: Hierholzer traversal consumes each ticket once and joins cycles through postorder. Exploring destinations in lexical order produces the smallest complete Euler trail, while reversing the finished-node list moves unavoidable dead ends to their proper final positions. Duplicate list entries represent distinct edges and must remain. The oracle independently tries all legal remaining-ticket choices and selects the minimum complete route.

tests.explanation: The tickets form JFK→MUC→LHR→SFO→SJC; all four flights are used once.
JFK→KUL is alphabetically first but ends too early. The complete route must be JFK→NRT→JFK→KUL.
